newsitem.title: CHINA: China, U.S. set date for new round of textile talks.
newsitem.headline: China, U.S. set date for new round of textile talks.

text.p: China and the United States have agreed to hold another round of talks on a new textile pact later this month in Beijing, the official Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
The two sides would discuss U.S. penalties imposed on imports of Chinese textiles and a Chinese threat to retaliate, the agency said.
Xinhua said the talks would begin on January 27.
In the previous round of negotiations in Washington last month, the U.S. side said it would re-examine its reduction of quotas for Chinese textiles, the news agency said.
Washington announced the penalties after accusing Chinese companies of shipping textiles through third countries to evade U.S. import quotas.

China has said it would postpone its retaliatory curbs on imports of some U.S. textiles, farm goods and alcoholic drinks until the end of this month. Those measures had been scheduled to go into effect on December 10 but were delayed to give the two sides more time for negotiation.
